text:
Lina: quick thread — ran activation-aware SmoothQuant (SQ) + AWQ comparisons on the new 13B model with 64k context. results are a bit noisy but worth discussing.
Sam: awesome, can you drop the key numbers?
Lina: baseline FP16 run (64k) — EM on long-qa eval: 72.3, avg ppl: 8.9, latency p95: 340ms/token.
Lina: AWQ-int8: EM 70.9 (-1.4), ppl 9.6 (+0.7), p95 210ms/token.
Lina: SmoothQuant (activation-aware) + int8 hybrid: EM 71.6 (-0.7), ppl 9.2 (+0.3), p95 230ms/token.
Sam: so AWQ is fastest but larger quality hit. SQ+int8 is middle ground.
Mike: what about GPTQ and FP8 runs?
Lina: GPTQ-4bit aggressive: EM 68.5 (-3.8), ppl 11.2 (+2.3). unstable on some QA templates.
Lina: FP8 (experimental kernels): EM 71.9 (-0.4), ppl 9.1 (+0.2), p95 180ms/token but memory footprint weird on a40.
Rachel: can you paste the exact command & config used so we can repro?
Lina: sure — full config in the run: ```bash
python eval_longctx.py \
  --model checkpoints/13B/fp16 \
  --quant awq|sq|fp8 \
  --ctx_len 65536 \
  --batch 1 \
  --kv_cache true \
  --activation_aware true \
  --seed 42
```
Sam: nice. any qual failures? examples?
Lina: yes — AWQ made some hallucination jumps on multi-hop where the activation distribution skews, example: it dropped the core entity in about 7/200 cases. SQ preserved core entity but paraphrased more.
Mike: do we have delta by prompt type? long-code vs long-story vs long-qa?
Lina: breakdown in drive: /drive/runs/1749854321/sq_awq_64k_report.md — TLDR: code-only prompts see ~0.5% EM delta, long-qa sees up to 2.5% for AWQ, narrative summarization ~0.8%.
quant-bot: nightly-eval finished: all runs logged to experiment-tracker (run ids: awq-1749, sq-1750, fp8-1751, gptq-1752).
Rachel: deployment implications? what's recommended for Dedicated vs Hosted?
Sam: for Dedicated (reserved GPUs) we prefer SQ+int8 as default profile: good quality, ~30% cost reduction vs fp16 and stable latency. AWQ as "fast path" could be enabled behind a rollout flag for read-heavy low-risk routes.
Mike: for Hosted API we should be conservative — maybe default fp16 and allow AWQ/FP8 as "burst" modes with automatic quality checks. fallback to fp16 on regression.
Lina: agreed. also enabling prefix/KV caching reduces the AWQ regret in production since many tokens are cached. we saw effective token-level cost down 42% when combining caching + SQ.
Sam: next steps?
Lina: 1) run longer seed sweep for FP8 memory quirks (CC: @Mike), 2) add prompt-type stratified eval to the compare notebook (CC: @Rachel), 3) wire small canary in Dedicated with SQ default and AWQ opt-in.
Rachel: will add checklist to rollout doc and alert thresholds.
Mike: i'll take the FP8 memory ticket, also will repro GPTQ instability with lower chunk sizes.
Lina: sweet — saved notebook + results are at the drive link above. ping me if you need raw logs. :rocket:
Sam: thanks — useful thread.
